results.name: Barbell Larsen Bench Press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your legs fully extended in front of your body and hold the barbell with a grip wider than shoulder width.
Keep your core tight and slowly lower the barbell to the middle of your chest while keeping your legs raised.
Pause briefly with the barbell lightly touching your chest.
Press the barbell back up until your arms are straight, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your legs fully extended and off the floor throughout the exercise, while engaging your core for stability.
Keep your wrists straight and stacked over your forearms.
Press the barbell in a smooth, controlled path over your chest and lower the weight slowly with control.
Inhale as you lower the barbell and exhale as you press it up.
results.description: Barbell Larsen Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Shoulders, Forearms.

results.name: Barbell Pullover to Triceps Extension
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing the barbell), hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Extend your arms so the barbell is directly above your chest.
Bend your elbows and lower the barbell in an arc motion behind your head. Lower the barbell until you feel a stretch in your chest and lats.
Reverse the motion by pulling the barbell back over your chest, then extend the barbell straight up by extending your arms fully.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily, inhaling as you lower the barbell and exhaling as you press it back up.
Use a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise to prevent strain or injury.
Ensure a firm grip on the barbell to maintain control and proper alignment.
results.description: Barbell Pullover to Triceps Extension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Barbell Reverse Close Grip Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a barbell with a reverse grip (palms facing back) and hands placed shoulder-width apart. Position the barbell directly above your chest with your arms fully extended.
Slowly lower the barbell towards your chest by bending your elbows. Keep your elbows close to your body throughout the movement.
Lower the barbell just before touching your chest, then push the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your body to ensure proper form and prevent shoulder strain.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Ensure a firm grip on the barbell to maintain control and proper alignment.
results.description: Barbell Reverse Close Grip Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Barbell Reverse Grip Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a barbell with a reverse grip (palms facing back) and hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Position the barbell directly above your chest with your arms fully extended.
Slowly lower the barbell towards your chest by bending your elbows. Keep your elbows close to your body throughout the movement.
Allow the barbell to lightly touch your chest, then push the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your body to ensure proper form and prevent shoulder strain.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Ensure a firm grip on the barbell to maintain control and proper alignment.
results.description: Barbell Reverse Grip Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Barbell Spoto Press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet firmly on the floor and hold the barbell above your chest with a shoulder width grip.
Lower the barbell slowly until it is just above your chest without allowing it to touch.
Pause briefly for 1 - 2 seconds while keeping the barbell steady above your chest.
Press the barbell back to the starting position with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and pressed into the bench, and your feet firmly planted on the floor for stability.
Maintain a straight bar path over your chest throughout the movement.
Keep the barbell just above your chest without letting it touch to maintain tension on the triceps. Pause briefly at the bottom of each repetition before pressing upward.
Inhale as you lower the barbell and exhale as you press it upward.
results.description: Barbell Spoto Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Core.

results.name: Barbell Wide Bench Press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet firmly planted on the floor. Hold a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing forward), hands placed wider than shoulder-width apart. Position the barbell directly above your chest with your arms fully extended.
Slowly lower the barbell to your chest by bending your elbows, keeping them at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Once the barbell lightly touches your chest, push the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your chest up and shoulders retracted throughout the movement to maximize chest engagement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it back down.
Keep your feet firmly planted on the floor for stability and support.
results.description: Barbell Wide Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Bodyweight Standing Fly
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended out to the sides, bent at 90 degrees, elbows at shoulder height.
Bring your arms together in front of your body until your forearms meet.
Open your arms back out to the sides to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your movements are smooth and controlled to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears to avoid tension.
Focus on squeezing your chest muscles as you bring your arms together to enhance muscle activation.
results.description: Bodyweight Standing Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Bodyweight Svend Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands pressed together close to your chest, elbows bent.
Extend your arms straight out in front of you, keeping your hands pressed together.
Bring your hands back to your chest, bending your elbows to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain a firm press of your hands together to engage your chest muscles throughout the exercise.
Keep your core engaged to maintain stability and balance.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
results.description: Bodyweight Svend Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Cable Bench Fly Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench positioned between two cable machines, with the cables set at a low position. Grasp the handles with your arms bent and hands close to your chest sides.
Press the handles upward in an arc motion over your chest, extending your arms upward.
Lower the handles back down to the starting position, stopping when your hands are close to your chest sides.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you press the handles up and inhale as you lower them back down.
Ensure your back remains flat against the bench and avoid arching your spine.
Focus on the contraction of your chest muscles as you press the handles up.
results.description: Cable Bench Fly Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Cable Core Palloff Press
instructions: Stand sideways to a cable machine with your feet shoulder width apart and hold the handle with both hands at chest level.
Press the handle straight forward until your arms are fully extended while resisting the cable's pull.
Pause briefly with your arms extended and keep your torso stable without rotating.
Bring the handle back to your chest with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.
tips: Keep your torso upright and avoid rotating during the movement.
Brace your core before pressing the handle forward.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees for better stability.
Inhale as you bring the handle toward your chest and exhale as you press it forward.
results.description: Cable Core Palloff Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.
